transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the materials review and production plan for the next window. As a reminder, we need to plan for 240 Model X motor drives and 120 Model Y motor drives. We currently have 600 power modules released for use, and I understand additional modules are physically present but sitting in a quality-hold area. Before I sign off on any allocation decisions, I need to hear from each of you: process engineering, quality, logistics, and product compliance. Let's walk through the current status and any constraints so we can finalize the plan together.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important from my engineering bill-of-materials review. I completed the review after the latest engineering change, and it confirms that each Model X drive requires exactly 2 power modules and each Model Y drive requires exactly 1 power module. However, I have not yet entered these revised quantities into the planning system, so the system may be showing outdated BOM data. Based on these confirmed figures, the full production plan of 240 Model X and 120 Model Y drives would require 600 power modules total — which exactly matches our currently released quantity.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from my inspection of the quality-hold area. I found that exactly 150 of the held modules can be recovered after a 6-hour controlled bake followed by insulation testing. I documented this result in a local inspection worksheet, but it has not yet been attached to the material record. This means we potentially have 150 additional modules beyond the 600 currently released, bringing the total to 750 — which could give us flexibility if the full production plan of 600 modules leaves no margin for issues.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share customer shipment confirmations I received by email but haven't yet posted to the shipment board. The Model X order can ship as 180 drives on Friday and 60 drives on Monday — it does not all need to ship Friday. However, the Model Y customer requires all 120 drives to ship on Friday. This means Friday's shipment requirement is 180 Model X drives and 120 Model Y drives, with the remaining 60 Model X drives following on Monday.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical compliance requirement from my destination review. Every Model Y drive must have serialized power-module traceability and a lot-specific compliance certificate before shipment. I completed the review for the export destination but have not yet added this requirement to the dispatch checklist. Since all 120 Model Y drives are required to ship on Friday per Jon's update, we need to ensure this traceability and certification requirement is satisfied before those shipments go out.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Enter the revised BOM quantities (2 modules per Model X, 1 per Model Y) into the planning system immediately so system data matches the confirmed engineering review.
Attach the local inspection worksheet documenting the 150 recoverable held modules to the material record so the recovery path is formally documented and available if needed.
Add the serialized power-module traceability and lot-specific compliance certificate requirement to the dispatch checklist for all Model Y drives before Friday shipment.
Verify that all 120 Model Y drives have serialized power-module traceability and lot-specific compliance certificates completed and approved before Friday shipment.
Post the customer shipment confirmations to the shipment board so the Friday (180 Model X + 120 Model Y) and Monday (60 Model X) schedule is visible to all teams.
If any issues arise with the 600 released modules during production, initiate the 6-hour controlled bake and insulation testing process to recover up to 150 held modules as backup.
